newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus plans deal with Kirch - paper.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus plans deal with Kirch - paper.

text.p: French pay television firm Canal Plus plans to swap its 37.5 percent interest in German pay TV channel Premiere for a 45 percent stake in Italy's Telepieu held by Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch, the French daily La Tribune said on Wednesday.
The report echoed a similar article that appeared in another French business newspaper, Les Echos, on Monday on which Canal Plus declined to comment.
Canal Plus would thereby raise its holding in Telepieu to 90 percent thanks to the 45 percent it already holds through its subsidiary Nethold, La Tribune said.
But it could dispose of part of its Telepieu stake to its partners such as public television company RAI, telecommunications operator Stet and other Italian investors, the newspaper said.
La Tribune quoted Canal Plus's managing director as saying its Italian talks were "very, very advanced".

Last weekend, a spokesman for Germany's Bertelsmann which holds the remaining 37.5 percent of Premiere said he was unaware of any deal between Canal Plus and Kirch but said such a move would have to approved by Bertelsmann.
The possibility of an accord has been flagged by executives of the three groups as necessary to allow the full development of digital services in Germany and Italy.
